title: Performance CLI and application projections
boundary_reason: Owns CLI behavior, application DTOs, adapter-neutral queries, runtime composition, and public summaries.
behavioral_concerns: Public projections must be bounded, sample-free, sanitized, and consistent across CLI, TUI, and web consumers.
Run and resume require confirmation; unsupported authority overrides and invalid flag combinations must fail as usage errors.
Text and JSON output must preserve stable schema, status, exit behavior, and stdout/stderr separation.

evidence.summary: Performance JSON encoding errors and text writer errors are explicitly ignored in the CLI adapter (qa-v1-block-a1c54f69a34aba9ad20c1302).
The current conformance review reports missing performance CLI compatibility coverage for JSON shape, output separation, and exit behavior (qa-v1-block-afc7f1a02ec78c68dd9233f4).

attempts.stop_reason: verification_unavailable: The CLI accepts a concrete sprint.Service and creates durable/runtime dependencies internally, so an approved app-package test cannot deterministically inject success, target_missed, cancelled, and partial RunPerformance outcomes without invoking the real performance workflow or modifying product source. The requested outcome branches therefore cannot all be reached with deterministic service and durable-operation fakes from the approved test path.. Required prerequisite: Provide an existing injectable performance command seam or approve a product-owned test adapter that controls PreparePerformance, RunPerformance, status projection, and durable-operation completion outcomes while retaining the real CLI envelope and exit translation.

verification_unavailable: The approved app test path cannot deterministically drive the concrete sprint.Service through successful, target_missed, cancelled, and partial RunPerformance branches. runSprintPerformance constructs and uses durable/runtime dependencies internally, and no injectable performance service or outcome seam exists. Reaching those branches would require the real workflow, contrary to the deterministic-fake requirement.. Required prerequisite: Provide or approve an existing test seam that injects performance preparation, durable ownership, runtime outcome, and status projection into the real CLI handler, enabling all four outcome branches without product-source changes or real runtime execution.

theories.claim: Performance CLI output failures are silently discarded because JSON encoding and text rendering write errors are ignored.
theories.basis: The performance command assigns away `json.Encoder.Encode` errors, while `renderSprintPerformance` ignores every `fmt.Fprintf` result; the error contract forbids disappearing failures and requires boundary adapters to preserve operational signals (qa-v1-block-a1c54f69a34aba9ad20c1302, qa-v1-block-307234c6bfff53948b392930).
theories.confirmation_condition: The implementation returns success or only the underlying operation error when writing the performance result to stdout fails.
theories.refutation_condition: The complete implementation propagates stdout encoding and rendering failures through another mechanism not visible in the excerpt.
theories.inconclusive_condition: The omitted command implementation wraps the shown output behavior so write failures cannot disappear.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Statically inspect the performance output closure and renderer, then use existing writer-failure test doubles if product-owned compatibility coverage is available.

theories.claim: The new performance CLI lacks compatibility tests covering stable JSON envelopes, stdout/stderr separation, and outcome-to-exit-code behavior.
theories.basis: The conformance review records this exact coverage gap, while the testing contract requires compatibility tests for public CLI response shapes, exit codes, output formats, and stable behavior (qa-v1-block-afc7f1a02ec78c68dd9233f4, qa-v1-block-cd1988b71fec72095e20320d).
theories.confirmation_condition: No compatibility test asserts the performance command's complete JSON envelope, stdout/stderr behavior, and semantic outcome exit mapping.
theories.refutation_condition: Existing tests explicitly cover those public contracts across representative terminal outcomes.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Relevant test bodies omitted from the frozen packet contain the asserted compatibility coverage.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Inspect only the named performance CLI test files or request an existing product-owned compatibility check ID.
